test_cases.title: Successful login redirects to dashboard within performance threshold
preconditions: User account exists with email verified
User is on the login page (Web, Android, iOS)
test_steps: Enter a correctly formatted email address belonging to an active user
Enter the correct password
Click the Login button
test_cases.expected_result: User is redirected to the dashboard URL, a session token/cookie is set, and the redirect completes in less than 2 seconds.
test_cases.automation_reason: All steps are UI actions with deterministic outcomes; can be automated using Selenium/Appium with performance timer hooks.

test_cases.title: Email format validation shows appropriate error
preconditions: User is on the login page
test_steps: Enter an email without '@' (e.g., 'invalidemail.com')
Enter any non‑empty password
Click the Login button
test_cases.expected_result: Email format error message is displayed, is visible, has ARIA role='alert', and does not disclose password status.
test_cases.automation_reason: Simple UI validation; can be captured via DOM inspection.

test_cases.title: Password field masking persists across platforms
preconditions: User is on the login page on Web, Android, and iOS
test_steps: Focus on the password input field
Type a password string
Inspect the input type attribute or visual representation
test_cases.expected_result: Password characters are masked (input type='password') on all platforms.
test_cases.automation_reason: Can be verified programmatically via WebDriver/Appium by checking element attributes.

test_cases.title: Generic error message displayed for incorrect credentials
preconditions: User is on the login page
test_steps: Enter a validly formatted email that exists in the system
Enter an incorrect password
Click the Login button
test_cases.expected_result: A generic authentication error message appears, is accessible (ARIA role='alert'), does not reveal whether email or password is wrong, and disappears after a successful login.
test_cases.automation_reason: Message text and attributes can be asserted via automated UI scripts.

test_cases.title: Brute‑force lockout after configurable failed attempts
preconditions: Lockout threshold is set to 5 failed attempts
test_steps: Repeat the following 5 times: enter valid email, enter wrong password, click Login
On the 6th attempt, enter the same credentials and click Login
test_cases.expected_result: After 5 failed attempts, the system returns a lockout notification; subsequent attempts continue to show lockout message until cooldown period expires.
test_cases.automation_reason: Looped UI actions can be scripted; lockout message can be validated.

test_cases.title: Login over TLS and no sensitive data logged
preconditions: Network traffic capture tool (e.g., Wireshark) is ready
Application logging is configured to mask passwords
test_steps: Start capture of HTTPS traffic
Perform a successful login with valid credentials
Stop capture and inspect packets
Review server logs for password leakage
test_cases.expected_result: All login requests are sent over TLS (HTTPS); no password or plaintext credentials appear in network capture or server logs.
test_cases.automation_reason: Requires network sniffing and log access, which are typically manual or require privileged integration.

test_cases.title: Login response time under load remains within SLA
preconditions: Baseline performance threshold: <2 seconds per login
test_steps: Simulate 200 concurrent login requests with valid credentials
Measure average response time for the login API
Verify that 95% of responses are under 2 seconds
test_cases.expected_result: Average login response time stays below 2 seconds; no error spikes or throttling unrelated to brute‑force protection.
test_cases.automation_reason: Can be fully automated with performance testing scripts.
